7429-trials-and-triumphs-of-faith.creator: Unknown

How God took her, healed her, and fitted her for his service, and how he used her as an instrument for his glory, is the story of her life.

arxiv-2102-00157.title: Zur Integration von Post-Quantum Verfahren in bestehende Softwareprodukte
arxiv-2102-00157.creator: Alexander Zeier, Alexander Wiesmaier, Andreas Heinemann
arxiv-2102-00157.description: Abstract \startpage 1 \editor \booktitle Beitrag für den 17. Deutschen IT-Sicherheitskongress, 2021 2021 Zusammenfassung Aktuell werden PQC-Algorithmen standardisiert, um der aufziehenden Gefahr für konventionelle asymmetrische Algorithmen durch Quantencomputer zu begegnen. Diese neuen Algorithmen müssen dann in bestehende Protokolle, Applikationen und Infrastrukturen eingebunden werden.

arxiv-2102-13104.title: Angular Distributions, Polarization Observables, Spin Density Matrices and Statistical Tensors in Photoproduction of Two Pseudoscalar Mesons off a Nucleon
arxiv-2102-13104.creator: Hiram G. Menendez Santiago
arxiv-2102-13104.description: Abstract In two meson photoproduction off a nucleon, for the case in which two of the three final state hadrons are products of the decay of an intermediate resonance, general expressions for its decay distribution and for polarization observables are derived in a model independent way.

arxiv-2103-06257.title: Maximum Entropy RL (Provably) Solves Some Robust RL Problems
arxiv-2103-06257.creator: Benjamin Eysenbach, Sergey Levine
arxiv-2103-06257.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Eysenbach, Sergey Levine. Many potential applications of reinforcement learning (RL) require guarantees that the agent will perform well in the face of disturbances to the dynamics or reward function. In this paper, we prove theoretically that maximum entropy (MaxEnt) RL maximizes a lower bound on a robust RL objective, and thus can be used to learn policies that are robust to some disturbances in the dynamics and the reward function.

arxiv-2207-04911.title: CougaR: Fast and Eclipse-Resilient Dissemination for Blockchain Networks DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: 16th ACM International Conference on Distributed and Event-Based Systems; June 27–30, 2022; Copenhagen, Denmark Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 Conference: The 16th ACM International
arxiv-2207-04911.creator: Evangelos Kolyvas, Spyros Voulgaris
arxiv-2207-04911.description: Abstract . Despite their development for over a decade, a key problem blockchains are still facing is scalability in terms of throughput, typically limited to a few transactions per second. A fundamental factor limiting this metric is the propagation latency of blocks through the underlying peer-to-peer network, which is typically constructed by means of random connectivity.

arxiv-2212-10981.title: On a manifold formulation of self-concordant functions
arxiv-2212-10981.creator: Hiroshi HIRAI
arxiv-2212-10981.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hiroshi HIRAI. In this paper, we address an extension of the theory of self-concordant functions for a manifold. We formulate the self-concordance of a geodesically convex function by a condition of the covariant derivative of its Hessian, and verify that many of the analogous properties, such as the quadratic convergence of Newton’s method and the polynomial iteration complexity of the path-following method, are naturally extended. However it is not known whether a useful class of self-concordant functions/barriers really exists for non-Euclidean manifolds.

arxiv-2304-00074.title: Bayesian Clustering via Fusing of Localized Densities
arxiv-2304-00074.creator: Alexander Dombowsky, David B. Dunson
arxiv-2304-00074.description: Abstract Bayesian clustering typically relies on mixture models, with each component interpreted as a different cluster. After defining a prior for the component parameters and weights, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms are commonly used to produce samples from the posterior distribution of the component labels.

arxiv-2402-03104.title: High-dimensional Bayesian Optimization via Covariance Matrix Adaptation Strategy
arxiv-2402-03104.creator: Lam Ngo s3962378@student.rmit.edu.au, Huong Ha huong.ha@rmit.edu.au, Jeffrey Chan jeffrey.chan@rmit.edu.au, Vu Nguyen vutngn@amazon.com, Hongyu Zhang hyzhang@cqu.edu.cn
arxiv-2402-03104.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lam Ngo s3962378@student.rmit.edu.au, Huong Ha huong.ha@rmit.edu.au, Jeffrey Chan jeffrey.chan@rmit.edu.au, Vu Nguyen vutngn@amazon.com, Hongyu Zhang hyzhang@cqu.edu.cn. Bayesian Optimization (BO) is an effective method for finding the global optimum of expensive black-box functions. However, it is well known that applying BO to high-dimensional optimization problems is challenging.

arxiv-2402-06781.title: A Survey of Four Precessing Waveform Models for Binary Black Hole Systems
arxiv-2402-06781.creator: Jake Mac Uilliam 1, Sarp Akçay 1, Jonathan E. Thompson 2
arxiv-2402-06781.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jake Mac Uilliam 1, Sarp Akçay 1, Jonathan E. Thompson 2. Angular momentum and spin precession are expected to be generic features of a significant fraction of binary black hole systems. As such, it is essential to have waveform models that faithfully incorporate the effects of precession. Here, we assess how well the current state of the art models achieve this for waveform strains constructed only from the ℓ = 2 \ell=2 multipoles.

arxiv-2405-07266.title: Architecture-Level Modeling of Photonic Deep Neural Network Accelerators
arxiv-2405-07266.creator: Tanner Andrulis, Gohar Irfan Chaudhry, Vinith M. Suriyakumar, Joel S. Emer, Vivienne Sze
arxiv-2405-07266.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tanner Andrulis, Gohar Irfan Chaudhry, Vinith M. Suriyakumar, Joel S. Emer, Vivienne Sze. Photonics is a promising technology to accelerate Deep Neural Networks as it can use optical interconnects to reduce data movement energy and it enables low-energy, high-throughput optical-analog computations. To realize these benefits in a full system (accelerator + DRAM), designers must ensure that the benefits of using the electrical, optical, analog, and digital domains exceed the costs of converting data between domains.

arxiv-2501-05399.title: Performance of YOLOv7 in Kitchen Safety While Handling Knife
arxiv-2501-05399.creator: Athulya Sundaresan Geetha Department of Computer Science, Huddersfield University, Queensgate, Huddersfield HD1 3DH, UK; * Correspondence: U2282847@unimail.hud.ac.uk;
arxiv-2501-05399.description: Abstract Safe knife practices in the kitchen significantly reduce the risk of cuts, injuries, and serious accidents during food preparation. Using YOLOv7, an advanced object detection model, this study focuses on identifying safety risks during knife handling, particularly improper finger placement and blade contact with hand. The model’s performance was evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95.

arxiv-2502-11722.title: Evidence for an accretion bridge in the DX Cha circumbinary system from VLTI/MATISSE observations
arxiv-2502-11722.creator: Tímea Juhász, József Varga, Péter Ábrahám, Ágnes Kóspál, Foteini Lykou, Lei Chen, Attila Moór, Fernando Cruz-Sáenz de Miera, Bruno Lopez, Alexis Matter, Roy van Boekel, Michiel Hogerheijde, Margaux Abello, Jean-Charles Augereau, Paul Boley, William C. Danchi, Thomas Henning, Mathis Letessier, Jie Ma
arxiv-2502-11722.description: Abstract DX Cha (HD 104237) is a spectroscopic binary consisting of a Herbig A7.5Ve-A8Ve primary star and a K3-type companion. Here we report on new 3.55 3.55 μ \upmu m interferometric observations of this source with the Multi Aperture Mid-Infrared Spectroscopic Experiment (MATISSE) at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI).

arxiv-2601-04157.title: FLEx: Language Modeling with F ew-shot L anguage Ex planations
arxiv-2601-04157.creator: Adar Avsian, Christopher Richardson, Anirudh Sundar, Larry Heck
arxiv-2601-04157.description: Abstract Language models have become effective at a wide range of tasks, from math problem solving to open-domain question answering. However, they still make mistakes, and these mistakes are often repeated across related queries. Natural language explanations can help correct these errors, but collecting them at scale may be infeasible, particularly in domains where expert annotators are required.

arxiv-2602-04604.title: Beyond Holistic Scores: Automatic Trait-Based Quality Scoring of Argumentative Essays
arxiv-2602-04604.creator: Lucile Favero, Juan Antonio Pérez-Ortiz, Tanja Käser, Nuria Oliver
arxiv-2602-04604.description: Abstract Automated Essay Scoring (AES) systems have traditionally focused on holistic scores, limiting their pedagogical usefulness, especially in the case of complex essay genres such as argumentative writing. In educational contexts, teachers and learners require interpretable, trait-level feedback that aligns with instructional goals and established rubrics.

pmc-11432833.title: 35 years after CLIA 1988: Key insights and policy implications among laboratory professionals
pmc-11432833.creator: Jaime A. Nieto Sierra, David Gefen
pmc-11432833.description: The Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) regulations of 1988 required certification of some clinical laboratory professionals but not of others. Analyzing survey data 35 years later, we explore how laboratory professionals today are inadvertently affected by those regulations, specifically their sense of professional identity and their perceptions of justice—and the consequences of those on their turnover intentions.

pmc-11674187.title: Inhibitory Effects of Cenobamate on Multiple Human Cardiac Ion Channels and Possible Arrhythmogenic Consequences
pmc-11674187.creator: Andreea Larisa Mateias, Florian Armasescu, Bogdan Amuzescu, Alexandru Dan Corlan, Beatrice Mihaela Radu
pmc-11674187.description: Cenobamate is a novel third-generation antiepileptic drug used for the treatment of focal onset seizures and particularly for multi-drug-resistant epilepsy; it acts on multiple targets: GABAA receptors (EC50 42–194 µM) and persistent neuronal Na+ currents (IC50 59 µM). Side effects include QTc interval shortening with >20 ms, but not <300 ms.

pmc-12403306.title: Comparative evaluation of surgicel and gelfoam in controlling post-extraction bleeding in patients on anticoagulant therapy: a clinical study
pmc-12403306.creator: Walaa AL-Suliman, Issa Wehbeh, Salim AL-hafyan
pmc-12403306.description: BackgroundBleeding after tooth extraction is a significant challenge, particularly in patients taking anticoagulants such as aspirin and warfarin, as the use of these medications increases the risk of prolonged bleeding. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the hemostatic agents, Surgicel and Gelfoam, in controlling bleeding and improving healing after extraction in this patient group.

pmc-12469346.title: Double-Network Hydrogels via Hybrid Strategies: Potential in Large-Scale Manufacturing for Colorimetric Indicator
pmc-12469346.creator: Ningli An, Jiwen Liu, Wentao Zhou, Qing He, Jianan Li, Yali Xiong
pmc-12469346.description: Biological hydrogels are widely available in terms of raw material sources and can be processed and molded using relatively simple techniques. Hydrogels can offer abundant three-dimensional, water-containing channels that facilitate the reaction between gases and dye, making them the preferred choice for the solid support layer in colorimetric indicators.

pmc-12532697.title: Go-or-grow models in biology: a monster on a leash
pmc-12532697.creator: Ryan Thiessen, Martina Conte, Tracy L Stepien, Thomas Hillen
pmc-12532697.description: Go-or-grow approaches represent a specific class of mathematical models used to describe populations where individuals either migrate or reproduce, but not both simultaneously. These models have a wide range of applications in biology and medicine, chiefly among those the modeling of brain cancer spread.

pmc-12622961.title: Treatment of Aorto-Oesophageal Fistula in a Tertiary German Aortic and Oesophageal Centre A Multidisciplinary Effort
pmc-12622961.creator: Felix Strobl, Jan Stana, Agnes Klara Böhm, Aldin Mehmedovic, Maximilian Pichlmaier, Hubert J Stein, Martin Angele, Nikolaos Tsilimparis
pmc-12622961.description: ObjectivesAlthough rare, aorto-oesophageal fistula remains one of the most critical diseases in cardiovascular surgery. The lack of prospective studies or large case series leads to an absence of evidence-based therapeutic concepts.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis of patients treated for aorto-oesophageal fistula between 2014 and 2023.

pmc-12650021.title: Aptamer-Based Strategies for Colorectal Cancer Detection: Emerging Technologies and Future Directions
pmc-12650021.creator: María Jesús Lobo-Castañón, Ana Díaz-Fernández
pmc-12650021.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with patient outcomes highly dependent on early and accurate diagnosis. However, existing diagnostic methods, such as colonoscopy, fecal occult blood testing, and imaging, are often invasive, costly, or lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity, particularly in early-stage disease.

pmc-12835178.title: Optimized deep learning for Indian Classical Dance Classification a novel application based on a refined version of chameleon swarm algorithm
pmc-12835178.creator: Di Zhu, Jinliang Sun, Yanwen Lu, Changiz Bastani
pmc-12835178.description: Indian Classical Dance (ICD) is a cultural art form much older than history, where the body movements convey emotions, spiritual meanings, or narrative meanings. Automated classification of ICD styles from visual data presents great challenges because of subtle inter-class variations, intra-class variations, and the complexity of human pose representation.

pmc-13009969.title: A retrospective real-world analysis of placental-based allografts on pressure ulcers
pmc-13009969.creator: David Kay, Marta Sandres-Corwin, Harry H Matundan
pmc-13009969.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective:The records from a network of mobile wound clinics were analyzed to evaluate the efficacy of a human placental-based allograft compared with the standard of care for patients with chronic pressure ulcer wounds and multiple comorbidities.Approach:Real-world evidence from a mobile wound clinic (July 2022–June 2023) was used to analyze patients with pressure ulcer wounds, most of whom received home-based wound care and had multiple comorbidities that worsened their chronic wounds.

pmc-13047398.title: Revision Hip Arthroplasty with a Single-Taper Cementless Conical Revision Stem: Clinical and Radiographic Assessment of 57 Implants
pmc-13047398.creator: Stefano Lucchini, Andrea Burla, Andrea Poletto, Francesco Castagnini, Simone Gerardi, Francesco Traina
pmc-13047398.description: BackgroundThe optimal stem design for revision hip arthroplasties is still controversial. A retrospective cohort study of revision hip arthroplasties performed using a single-taper cementless conical stem was designed, aiming to assess clinical outcomes, complications and survival rates, and radiological osseointegration, at a minimum follow-up of 2 years.

pmc-13243338.title: The Role of Physical Activity in the Prevention and Management of Obesity: A Position Statement From the World Obesity Federation
pmc-13243338.creator: Zoe Gowers, Bai Li, Santi F Gómez, Angela Jackson‐Morris, Mychelle Farmer, Rachel Thompson, Kent Buse
pmc-13243338.description: This position statement is intended to synthesize and interpret current consensus and salient developments regarding the relationship between obesity and physical activity. It draws from the latest evidence and guidelines to update and share the World Obesity Federation's stance with policymakers, healthcare professionals, public health stakeholders, and civil society organizations.

pmc-13473119.title: Exploring multiple minimal clinically important differences for the esophageal cancer scale QLICP-ES (V2.0) based on anchor-based and distribution-based methods
pmc-13473119.creator: Jianfeng Tan, Ting Wu, Fengbo Guo, Gaofeng Li, Jiudi Zhong, Yujing Fang, Chonghua Wan
pmc-13473119.description: The minimal clinically important difference (MCID) is an important phrase with big appeal in the interpretation of quality of life (QOL), and a bridge between statistical inference and clinical implication. This study aimed to explore multiple MCIDs of the QLICP-ES(V2.0), an esophageal cancer scale in Quality of Life Instruments system for Cancer Patients.

pmc-13505588.title: Precision Oncology via Radiotherapy‐Triggered Drug Delivery: Mechanisms, Molecular Engineering, and Clinical Translation
pmc-13505588.creator: Jianv Jiang, Tanfeng Zhang, Junliang Dong, Wenjing Sun
pmc-13505588.description: Radiotherapy‐triggered drug delivery systems (RDDS) promise to integrate the spatial precision of ionizing radiation with controllable pharmacological activation. However, clinical translation remains constrained by its reliance on supra‐clinical irradiation doses. Here, we present a unifying framework redefining RDDS through two distinct paradigms: structural disassembly and molecular actuation.

pmc-13632583.title: CrSbSe3 Nanowire: A Platform for Near-Perfect Spin Selectivity
pmc-13632583.creator: Alyssa Horne, Yongmei M. Jin, Ranjit Pati
pmc-13632583.description: Spin-selective carrier transport in low-dimensional magnetic semiconductors is central to the development of next-generation spintronics. However, achieving robust spin-filtering together with long spin-coherence under nonequilibrium conditions remains a major challenge. Recently isolated by top-down exfoliation, the CrSbSe3 nanowire has emerged as a ferromagnetic semiconductor exhibiting enhanced coercivity compared to its bulk counterpart.
